Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Jonah: i tested the courtyard version this morning. the first two directions are fine, but the recording calls the room “the old harbor gallery” and the new wall label says “Harbor Stories.” visitors will probably think those are two different places. i can swap the room name in the script; the object numbers and timing don't need to change. also, the little arrow on screen points toward the stairs when you're standing by the courtyard door. it needs to point left toward the main hall, not down to the basement. i'll send a screenshot after lunch so design can see the angle.

Priya: quick note from the listening station, the right earbud on handset 14 cuts out if you bend the cable near the plug. i've put a yellow tag on it and left it in the charging drawer, not on the public rack. there are twelve other units charged and working, and the spare pair from the education cupboard is still there if we need it for the school group. could someone update the checkout sheet so the front desk doesn't hand out 14 by accident? i haven't removed it from the inventory list yet because i don't know if repair can get to it before opening.

Eli: for the script review, i'm on the section about the brass compass. the draft says it belonged to Captain Vale, but the accession card only says it was donated by his granddaughter, Nora Vale, in 1978. that's not the same as saying he owned it, so i'd keep the voiceover to what the record confirms. we could say, “The compass came to the museum from Nora Vale in 1978.” there's a nice detail about the scratched initials on the back, but the catalog doesn't identify them, so let's not guess who they belonged to. i'll check the final recording against the label tomorrow.

Mara: yep, thanks. let's keep the compass wording close to the card. for the courtyard sign, design can use the same blue arrow as the map, but please don't put the entrance number on it because that number is only used for deliveries. here's the order i have for the opening checks:
1. test the route from both doors
2. listen to the room-name change on handset 3
3. check the arrow on a phone held upright
4. leave the tagged handset out of circulation
if we can get through those before the school visit, the staff briefing will be a lot less confusing. i'll bring the printed route sheet to the desk.

Lena: i tried the route with the screen reader enabled, and the stop names are read in the right order. the only snag is the button says “play stop” but the voice prompt says “listen here”; i think we should use one phrase for both, otherwise people may wonder if they're doing different things. the volume slider also resets to halfway when you close the guide and reopen it. that seems okay for the demo phone, but our visitors often share devices, so the next person may get a much quieter guide than expected. can the app remember the last setting just for that visit?

Jonah: design sent the sign proof over. it has the blue arrow and no delivery number, so that part matches. the text is a bit small from the bench by the courtyard, though; i checked from where a wheelchair user would wait and had to roll closer to read it. could we increase the lettering without making the sign wider? the stone panel beside it has a narrow edge and the facilities team asked us not to cover the brass plaque. i've marked the safe area on the proof, and the panel can still be read from the path if we keep the lower corner clear.

Priya: front desk has the updated checkout sheet now, and i told them handset 14 is tagged for repair. the spare pair is still in the education cupboard, so it can go with the school group if their teacher asks. one other thing, two visitors asked whether the guide has captions for the short audio clips. it does, but the captions are hidden behind the small “CC” icon on the player. maybe the welcome card should mention that, since the icon isn't obvious to everyone. i can add one line to the staff notes, but i won't change the printed card unless we agree on the wording.

Eli: last update for today: the sound check in the carved boat room is booked for friday at 8:15, before the doors open. the cleaning team will still be in the east corridor then, so the test group should enter by the west doors and follow the route in reverse to avoid the wet floor. the school group arrives at 10:00, and their teacher asked for the guide to be ready in English and Spanish. the Spanish track is already on the server; we'll check the first stop and the compass section during the sound check.
